subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm examining the renders to find the lowest point of the geometry, tracing through the base cylinder, boot soles, and rock icosahedron dimensions to figure out where the bottom extends to around 46mm below y=0.

I adjust the rock placement math so the scaled icosahedron sits with its bottom closer to the ground plane, settling on a y-offset around s*0.85 to keep things within tolerance.

Then I shift to checking the dwarf's pose, noting the blunderbuss is held with the right arm raised toward the viewer at roughly a 40-degree upward angle, and start evaluating whether that placement actually looks right.

The gun looks thin and the left arm hangs stiffly by the sign — I try to calculate whether the left hand could instead support the gun's fore-end, but the geometry puts it too far across the body to reach, so I decide to leave the arm mostly as-is with maybe a slight outward bend, prioritizing more impactful fixes.

Looking at the head, I realize the face is too busy — tiny eyes get lost behind an oversized beard, cheek blobs, and a clownish red nose sphere, so I plan to enlarge the eye decals and adjust the brow to help the face read more clearly.

I'm also checking the cheek blobs, which fuse with the nose into a trio of red balls, so I want to shrink and desaturate them while tweaking the nose color slightly less red.

The shoulder pauldrons being big and blobby actually fits the Warcraft aesthetic, so I'll leave those alone, and the hood and neck look fine too.

Checking the side view, the pack appears detached from the body with a visible gap, so I'm running through the z-depth math for the chest blob and pack placement to see if they should actually be touching, wondering if a hunched torso lean is what's creating the illusion of separation.

Now I'm looking at the gold ring near the pack (likely a rope coil or canteen attachment), which reads fine sticking out to the side.

The knee guards are oversized silver spheres that look like big balls stuck on the thighs, so I want to shrink them and flatten them into disc-shaped guards instead, keeping the steel color but adjusting scale and offset so they read as knee plates rather than balls—this is likely due to foreground perspective exaggerating their size. I'm also noting the boot soles look like dark floating boxes extending past the boots themselves.

Checking the dark slabs under the boots that resemble skateboard decks — I'll narrow them and switch to a darker leather brown so they blend into the boot rather than sticking out as separate plates. The helmet crest, goggles, brass band, beard, and left hand all look acceptable as-is. The gun's position in the three-quarter view, passing in front of the beard and chest with the hand gripping the lower stock, also reads fine, though I'm checking where the stock end lands relative to the back.

The gun looks too thin and stick-like in the front view, so I'm bumping up the barrel radius and enlarging the bell at the end for better visual weight. I'm also trying to reposition the sign on the base so it's not obscured by the left arm in the front view, running through coordinate math to find a spot within the base's elliptical boundary where the sign board won't overlap the hand.

Adjusting rock ring radii and base cylinder dimensions to match the shifted post position...

Checking the crate and keg placement near the signpost — they're spaced enough apart, so I just need to shift the sign's x-coordinate by 0.1 while keeping the post and texture plane z-values as they are.

I also want to reconsider the Warcraft-style exaggeration — chunkier proportions, bigger hands — though the right hand fingers look fine so I might leave that alone. Then I'm adjusting the left arm's pose, moving the elbow outward and recalculating the reach distance from the shoulder joint to make it look less stiff.

Checking the pack's bedroll detail and the tabard — those seem fine as is.

The mouth stays hidden by the beard, so I'll skip that. I'm enlarging the eyes slightly and adjusting their position relative to the brow blobs so they don't overlap awkwardly, then placing a cheek blob with a warm skin tone slightly behind the main face plane for subtle shading.

Now I'm widening the rock ring and base cylinder radii outward so the rocks sit further from center, bumping up the floor slab's bottom offset and rock-tilt randomization to make the terrain look more natural.

Checking the sign post coordinates and wood/snow/iron trim positions need shifting from 0.5 to 0.6 along the support, then moving on to the knee guard blob placements for the figure.

I'm resizing the knee guard blob and torus, swapping the foot sole box to a smaller leather material, enlarging the eye decals with more segments, adjusting the nose color and scale, tweaking the left arm target coordinates, and now modifying the gun barrel's lathe profile points.

Adjusting barrel thickness and ring radii...
